column3: NASB follows the critical text (“also … to Lystra”) without “certain” before “woman.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB follows the critical text; “This one” is rendered “this man.”
NASB follows the critical text without “the” before “elders”; it moves “to keep” to the end as “for them to observe.”
NASB renders “every day” as “daily.”
NASB follows the critical text (“passed through”); it renders the phrase as “the Phrygian and Galatian region.”
NASB follows the critical text with “the Spirit of Jesus.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB follows the critical text; “beseeching” is rendered “appealing to.” A full-width colon appears in the NASB text.
NASB follows the critical text (“God”); “evangelize” is rendered “preach the gospel.”
NASB renders “having sailed” as “putting out to sea.”
NASB follows the critical text with “a leading city of the district”; it adds “Roman.”
NASB follows the critical text (“gate”); it renders the clause as “we were supposing that there would be a place of prayer.” The meaning of the clause is uncertain.
NASB adds “fabrics,” renders “attend to” as “respond to,” and reorders the verse.
NASB follows the critical text; “begged” is rendered “urged,” and “persuaded” is “prevailed upon.”
NASB follows the critical text; it renders “a spirit, a python” as “a spirit of divination” and “girl” as “slave-girl.”
NASB follows the critical text (“to you”); “servants” is rendered “bond-servants.”
NASB follows the critical text; “distressed” is rendered “greatly annoyed,” and “hour” is “moment.”
NASB renders “rulers” as “authorities.”
NASB renders “magistrates” as “chief magistrates” and “exceedingly trouble” as “throwing … into confusion.”
NASB renders “practice” as “observe.” A stray quotation mark appears in the NASB text.
NASB renders “garments” as “robes” and “were commanding” as “proceeded to order.”
NASB renders “strictly” as “securely.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB renders “singing praises” as “singing hymns of praise.”
NASB follows the critical text; “of all the chains” is rendered “everyone's chains.”
NASB follows the critical text; it renders “awoken” as “roused out of sleep” and “execute” as “kill.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB renders “terrified having become” as “trembling with fear.”
NASB renders “what is necessary for me to do” as “what must I do.”
